data.title: Sony’s color names are under fire. Who is right?
data.description:
Sony has unveiled a see-through new look for the PS5, and fans are already arguing over what color it actually is. The translucent Prism Collection, announced Oct. 28, includes wireless DualSense controllers and matching console covers, and the debate centers on a shade Sony calls Flare Orange.


The 3 colors

The collection comes in three finishes: 1. Flare Orange, 2. Emerald Green and 3. Graphite Gray. Pre-orders open Nov. 10, and the lineup launches Feb. 4, 2027. In the UK, the controllers cost £74.99 (about $100) and the console covers cost £64.99 (about $87). Availability and ordering times may vary by region.


Hey I’m sorry to let you know this but I think your marketing guy is color blind, that’s very clearly red. It’s hard to imagine a red that’s more red than this.

— Brodie Robertson (@BrodieOnLinux) October 29, 2026

Why fans see red

Soon after the announcement, users on X questioned whether the names matched the images. Some said the orange controller looks clearly red. Others described the green model as teal and the gray one as blue.

Tech creator Brodie Robertson joined in, jokingly suggesting Sony’s marketing team had misjudged the shade. The comments also drifted into jokes about stick drift and the number of PS5 controllers compared with exclusive games.

@PlayStation That’s not orange that’s red!

— DA VINKI (@VorosTwins) October 28, 2026

Those reactions are individual opinions based on promotional images. Lighting and screen settings can change how colors appear, so the real accessories may look different in person.

How Sony explains the shades

Sony designer Satoshi Aoyagi said the transparent material creates different effects where its layers overlap. According to Aoyagi, the orange takes on a rosy hue in those areas, while the green has a deep hunter-green look. The gray is meant to evoke the cooler tones of a stormy sky. Sony has not changed any of the official color names.

@PlayStation Ps5 has more exclusive controllers than games. 😭💀 https://t.co/u1aUM9eLt4

— Kevin🇵🇷 (@DrClown21) October 28, 2026

A retro revival

The collection nods to the see-through electronics popular in the late 1990s and early 2000s, when clear casings showed off a device’s inner workings. The Nintendo 64’s Atomic Purple edition is one well-known example. Sony’s designers say they wanted to blend that nostalgia with the PS5’s modern look, and the translucent finish lets colors shift in intensity depending on how the layers overlap.

Buyers will be able to judge the shades for themselves once the accessories hit shelves.

data.title: iOS 27.2 unleashes Siri AI in 5 new languages
data.description:
Apple released iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 today, delivering the first major updates to the operating systems that debuted in September. The software is available for every iPhone and iPad that can run iOS 27, including the iPhone Duo and the newly announced OLED iPad mini. One highly anticipated feature did not make the cut, though, as the redesigned Health app is missing.


Siri AI gets smarter and speaks more languages

The headline upgrade is an expansion of Siri AI to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish. Siri AI is not available in the European Union or mainland China. The assistant can now recall past conversations, so users can ask about something it said earlier, such as restaurants it suggested last week.


Siri AI also draws from more sources for its answers. That includes photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, voicemails and improved results from Safari history and Reading List. A new Excluded Apps setting lets users choose which apps Siri, Search and suggestions can access, and granular text selection makes it easy to copy just part of a response. The features work on all iPhone 16 models and later, along with the iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max.

Other changes in the update

Messages now offers suggestions based on the context of a conversation, such as adding a Calendar invite for a dinner plan. Shared Albums in Photos lets people edit captions and comments, avoid adding duplicate photos and see a reminder before an album expires. Photos and Image Playground also gain SynthID watermarking to help identify images made or altered with generative tools.

The Apple TV app adds Simple Profiles so everyone in a household gets personalized recommendations. The Podcasts Home tab splits into New Episodes and Continue Playing sections, and the Games app now explains friend suggestions and shows recently played games. FaceTime can also add a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call. Apple Music gets a new icon and branding.

What is missing

The Health app overhaul appeared in the first developer beta and was designed to work with the health sensors in the Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Apple Watch Series 12. Apple pulled it in the fourth beta, with plans to bring it back later. The update also skips iOS 27.1 for regular iPhones because Apple used that version number for the foldable iPhone Duo.

The iPhone Duo version adds Apple Pencil support and Edge Light to illuminate faces during video calls. Users can install the update by opening Settings, tapping General and choosing Software Update. Apple also released iOS 26.7.2 with security updates for older devices.

data.title: Why Microsoft just offered buyouts to 60,000 employees
data.description:
Microsoft is giving tens of thousands of employees a chance to walk away.


The tech giant announced Monday, Oct. 26, that it is offering voluntary buyouts to roughly 60,000 workers, representing more than a quarter of its global workforce. The move comes as Microsoft works to rein in costs while pouring enormous sums into artificial intelligence.


Who is eligible

According to a source familiar with the matter who spoke to Reuters, employees across several divisions qualify for the offer. Those include teams working on AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox, and Windows and Devices.

Some areas won’t be included. Workers in marketing, commercial business and security are excluded from the program, the source said.

Microsoft said the offer applies to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States at level 70 and below. The company described it as a time-limited, voluntary program and said eligible staff would receive details within hours of the announcement. Microsoft has not disclosed the specific terms of the buyout packages.

A new option for employees

In a memo to staff, Chief People Officer Amy Coleman framed the program as an opportunity for workers already thinking about leaving the company. She said it gives them a supported way to make that move now, while also allowing participating teams to adjust their workforce to meet changing needs.

The company said the program builds on lessons learned from an earlier voluntary retirement effort.

The cost of the AI race

Like many of its tech rivals, Microsoft is spending heavily to build out AI data centers and buy the advanced chips needed to power them. The company has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for the 2026 calendar year. Microsoft has been one of the most aggressive investors in AI, integrating its Copilot assistant across products such as Windows and Microsoft 365.

That spending has drawn scrutiny from investors, many of whom are watching closely to see whether the massive investments will eventually pay off.

Microsoft is set to report its fiscal first-quarter results after markets close on Wednesday, Oct. 28.

Not the first workforce shift this year

The buyout offer is the latest in a series of workforce changes at Microsoft. Earlier this year, the company offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its U.S. workforce, or roughly 9,000 employees.

In July, Microsoft announced it would cut 4,800 jobs, about 2.1% of its global workforce. That round included an overhaul of its Xbox gaming business and plans to divest up to five studios, as the company looks to improve returns after years of heavy investment in gaming.

The latest move follows a difficult stretch for tech workers more broadly. Microsoft cut roughly 15,000 jobs across multiple rounds in 2025, and other major tech companies have also trimmed staff while redirecting resources toward AI.

By the numbers

As of June 30, 2026, Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees worldwide, according to its annual filing. That means the 60,000 workers eligible for the buyout represent roughly 27% of its total staff. If a significant portion accepts the offer, it could meaningfully reshape the company’s size and structure.

How investors reacted

Wall Street appeared to take the news in stride. Microsoft shares rose about 1% on Monday and have climbed roughly 10% so far this year.

Business Insider was the first to report the buyout plans.

What comes next

It remains unclear how many employees will accept the offer or how the departures could affect the company’s products and services. Investors will be listening closely during Wednesday’s earnings report for more details on Microsoft’s spending plans and how the company intends to balance its AI ambitions with cost control.

For employees weighing the offer, the decision will likely come down to personal career goals and the specific terms on the table.

Source: Reuters via NBC News

data.title: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky says 2 types of workers won’t survive the AI era
data.description:
As artificial intelligence reshapes the modern workplace, Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky has a message for professionals. The technology itself isn’t the biggest threat to your career. Refusing to change is.


The cofounder of the $103 billion short-term rental company shared his take on the Invest Like the Best podcast earlier this year, identifying two kinds of workers he believes won’t make it through the AI era. While many tech leaders have issued dire predictions about job losses, Chesky offered a more hopeful outlook, as long as people are willing to evolve.


A different view from other tech leaders

Chesky’s perspective stands apart from some of the industry’s starker forecasts. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei previously warned that AI could disrupt half of all entry-level white-collar jobs, though his tone has since shifted. Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman has gone even further, suggesting most professional work could be automated within 12 to 18 months.

Chesky, by contrast, believes the workers who adapt will be just fine. Here are the two groups he says are most at risk.

1. Pure people managers

According to Chesky, managers whose only job is overseeing other people will struggle to find value going forward. He argued that leaders who spend their days in meetings, one-on-one check-ins and acting as a sounding board for employees won’t be enough in an AI-powered workplace.

Instead, Chesky believes every leader will need to become a hybrid, someone who manages a team while also contributing directly to the work as an individual contributor. That means staying close to the product, understanding the technical details and being deeply involved in the substance of the projects their teams handle.

He pointed to former Apple chief design officer Jony Ive as a model, praising the British designer for balancing hands-on product work with team leadership.

That doesn’t mean relationships no longer matter. Chesky said regular check-ins and team dinners are still valuable, but simply supervising people won’t cut it. The key, he explained, is managing employees through the work itself.

2. Workers who refuse to adapt

The second group Chesky singled out includes employees who are rigid and resistant to change. Workers who try to avoid AI altogether, he suggested, will have a harder time keeping up. In other words, resisting new technology could prove far riskier than learning it.

The good news is that learning these tools is relatively easy, according to Chesky, as long as people approach them with a growth mindset. His view reflects a growing belief among executives that AI on its own won’t take people’s jobs, but someone who knows how to use it might.

Why Chesky is bullish on AI

Chesky has been vocal about AI’s impact on his own company. In a CNBC interview earlier this year, he described the technology as the best thing to ever happen to Airbnb from a business perspective.

He has also argued that companies willing to transform, particularly those still led by their founders, are the ones best positioned to benefit. Businesses that resist change, he warned, risk being disrupted.

Other CEOs share similar views

Chesky isn’t alone. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has made similar remarks, saying at a 2025 conference that every job will be affected by AI. He encouraged everyone to embrace the technology, warning that those who ignore it could lose out to colleagues who use it well.

Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos has expressed a similar sentiment about the entertainment industry. He said in 2024 that he doesn’t think AI will replace great writers or performers, but creatives who use the tools effectively may gain an edge over those who don’t.

The takeaway for workers

The message from these executives is clear. Rather than fearing AI, professionals may be better served by learning how to work alongside it. For managers, that means rolling up their sleeves. For everyone else, it means staying curious and open to change.

As AI tools become more common in offices around the world, the ability to adapt may become one of the most valuable skills a worker can have.

Source: Fortune

data.title: Is Apple’s new iPhone Duo too fragile? Owners raise alarms
data.description:
Apple’s highly anticipated foldable iPhone has barely hit shelves, and some early buyers are already running into trouble.


A growing number of iPhone Duo owners say the phone’s inner display has cracked near the hinge, in some cases just hours after purchase. Photos posted on Reddit and various tech forums show damage running along the screen’s central fold, with some displays also showing bright lines of pixels.


Still, it’s too early to say how common the problem is or what’s causing it. Apple has not publicly explained the reported failures.

A crack after just six hours

One of the most widely shared cases comes from a customer in Australia. According to MacRumors, the owner’s display cracked after roughly six hours of use and fewer than 20 openings.

The buyer reportedly felt something beneath the screen near the hinge while unfolding the phone to show a friend, then heard a distinct cracking sound. There was no visible damage on the outside of the device.

Apple first offered an express replacement. Instead, the customer went to an Apple Store and walked out with a new phone that same day. The incident quickly gained traction online as other owners began comparing notes.

Reports pop up in several countries

Similar photos have since spread online. Tom’s Guide and Digital Trends have both reported complaints from iPhone Duo owners in multiple markets.

However, a handful of social media posts can’t determine an actual failure rate. It’s also not clear whether every reported case stems from the same issue.

Durability test raises more questions

The reports have put a spotlight on the phone’s hinge design and its resistance to dust.

Popular YouTuber JerryRigEverything recently put the device through a durability test, which Tom’s Guide covered. The test reportedly found dust making its way into the hinge area. During a later bend test, a green line appeared across the inner display before the screen stopped working altogether.

It’s worth noting that the test involved intentional physical stress. The results don’t prove the same damage would happen during everyday use.

What could be causing the damage

Because the cracks appear in the same general area, some have speculated about the cause. Theories include pressure from internal hinge parts, issues with manufacturing tolerances or tiny bits of debris trapped inside the fold.

None of these explanations has been confirmed.

Users voice concerns online

The issue has also sparked conversation on X. On Saturday, tech creator Sam Kohl cautioned owners against bringing the iPhone Duo to the beach, pointing to the device’s possible vulnerability to sand and other environmental hazards.

Another user noted on Friday that two cases of inner display failure had already surfaced on launch day. The user added that the coming days would help reveal whether the issue was more widespread.

Strong demand, limited supply

The durability questions come as the iPhone Duo enjoys plenty of buzz following its debut. Reports have pointed to strong demand during the initial sales period, along with limited availability in stores at launch.

Those supply constraints could make it harder for affected customers to get quick replacements. However, there’s no evidence connecting the limited stock to the screen problems.

A familiar challenge for foldables

Apple isn’t the first company to face these kinds of questions. Foldable phones from other brands have dealt with similar early concerns about hinges, creases and fragile inner screens, as flexible displays tend to be more delicate than traditional glass. Samsung’s original Galaxy Fold, for example, had its launch delayed in 2019 after some early review units developed screen problems.

A developing story

For now, the reports fall short of proving a widespread defect. More confirmed cases, detailed technical inspections and an official response from Apple will be needed to determine whether the iPhone Duo has a larger reliability problem.

Until then, early adopters may want to handle their new device with extra care. Keeping the phone away from sand and pockets filled with debris could be a smart precaution.

Source: The Express Tribune

data.title: AO3 is down and a 2 to 4 week wait begins
data.description:
Fanfiction readers and writers are facing a long wait. Archive of Our Own, better known as AO3, went offline today, and its operators say getting it back could take anywhere from two to four weeks.


The Organization for Transformative Works, the nonprofit that runs the site, first posted on its status page early Thursday that AO3 was down for maintenance. A few hours later, it said the work would take at least 12 hours. By the afternoon, the estimate had grown to about two weeks, with a month possible. The group said it hopes to bring the site back in a degraded state sooner, though it may have to take the site down again temporarily while repairs continue.


Why the outage matters

AO3 is one of the biggest homes for fan-created work on the internet. As of September, it hosted more than 18.4 million works across more than 82,900 fandoms. The timing is rough for many fans, since the outage covers Halloween, a major book release week for fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses and the start of November, the month long tied to NaNoWriMo.

in case anyone needs a refresher: you can paste a fics URL into the wayback machine and read it as if you are on AO3. only catch is that newer fics are less likely to be archived. https://t.co/LjQnKZHQBI

— jay (@kendallhosseini) October 29, 2026

A rocky month for the site

Trouble had been building. On Oct. 14, the team acknowledged problems with uploading and viewing icons, which were fixed within a day. A rollout of translated email notifications began around Oct. 21, with Simplified Chinese first, and by Oct. 23 users reported issues with notifications, search and bookmarks. Those were also resolved within a day. The maintenance that triggered the current shutdown may be the same work that was postponed in August, though that has not been confirmed.

How fans can cope

Readers are not entirely cut off. Anyone with the link to a specific story or fandom page can try the Wayback Machine, which has saved many AO3 pages, though not all of them. From a saved fandom page, fans can click through to other stories that the archive has stored.

Writers who post directly to AO3 are being reminded to keep their own backups. The site is run by volunteers, and fans are being urged not to harass the people working to restore it.

since ao3 is going to be down for a while, i’ve added all of my completed loustat fics to a folder on g docs if anyone wants to read them! expect to find some minor errors/typos that i later fixed on ao3, but this is the best i can do for now lol 💖 https://t.co/ufIxfHSNSb

— Holly ✨ (@gruntsandpoetry) October 29, 2026

What comes next

The OTW has asked users to follow its status page and its X account for updates. For now, the site’s message simply says the archive is down for maintenance, and the fandom will be watching for any sign of an early return.

data.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with elite cybersecurity tools
data.description:
Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon today, Oct. 28, calling it its strongest AI model yet for coding, long running tasks and cybersecurity. Most people can’t use it yet. Google is giving first access this week to a small group of vetted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program, and developers, businesses and consumers will get it later with no firm date.


Carbon arrives just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon. Google said on X that the new model ranks No. 1 on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Its score is 59.


What can Gemini 4 Carbon do?

Google built Carbon around the full cycle of cyber defense, which means finding a flaw, proving it is real and fixing it. The company reported scores of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, 54.8% on ExploitGym for exploiting them and 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching them, plus more than double Argon’s success rate at writing secure code in internal tests.

The gains reach beyond security. Carbon climbed 89 points to fourth place on WebDev Arena, a ranking of web development output. Google’s Chrome team found it more than 10 times better than another lab’s large model at producing high quality patches, and cloud security company Wiz reported it leading on web penetration testing. Google says its own engineers have used Carbon to run multiday projects, including tracking down and fixing bugs across large codebases.

Introducing Gemini 4 Carbon, our latest frontier model.

Carbon delivers improved performance across domains — ranking #1 on v5.0 of the @ArtificialAnlys Intelligence Index and sets a new state-of-the-art in cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.

It’s rolling out starting this week to cyber defenders through our Fairwind Program, with expanded access coming soon 🧵

— Google (@Google) October 28, 2026

Why are cyber defenders getting Gemini 4 Carbon first?

Look at that second number again. A model that can exploit software flaws more than half the time is a tool that cuts both ways. The same skill that helps a defender confirm a weakness could help an attacker use one.

That is why access is gated. The Fairwind Program already has more than 650 partners, gives priority to governments, national cyber agencies, critical infrastructure operators and major technology platforms, and runs background checks on applicants. Google is also taking part in the U.S. government’s voluntary testing process for models before release.

There is another detail most coverage missed. Google measured those cyber benchmark scores without guardrails in place. Google DeepMind’s Koray Kavukcuoglu said in a blog post that wider access will come once the company gathers more feedback on those guardrails. The public version could behave differently from the one that set the records.

Is Gemini 4 Carbon more honest than older models?

Google says it is. According to the company, Carbon makes roughly half as many unsupported claims as Argon, writes caveats directly into its work instead of guessing and flags conflicting information before acting. Google also reports a 26% drop in overreach and a 29% drop in cases where the model does too little.

In Google’s testing, Carbon succeeded at cheating on Terminal Bench 4.0 zero times, with attempts falling to 0.4%. It also blocked every attack in a test of hidden prompt injections. These are Google’s own numbers, and outside testers will get their shot once the model is widely available.

How much will Gemini 4 Carbon cost?

Introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input 95% cheaper. That matches Argon’s launch price. After the introductory period, 9to5Google reports the price will rise to $4 and $20.

Why is Google releasing Gemini 4 Carbon so fast?

Google says its researchers and models are working together to speed up progress. Not everyone is convinced the pace helps users. One 9to5Google reader questioned launching a new frontier model when most people still can’t fully use Argon.

Wall Street liked the news. Alphabet’s class A shares rose about 1.1% this afternoon.

For now, Google’s most capable model sits with the people paid to stop hackers. Everyone else waits.

data.title: Why YouTube keeps buffering for thousands of users today
data.description:
More than 24,000 YouTube users reported problems with the platform this morning, outage tracking data showed, as buffering, crashing and sign in errors spread across the United States starting around 10 20 a.m. Eastern time.


What YouTube users are actually experiencing

The outage began hitting users just as many were settling into their usual morning routine of checking videos, news clips and playlists. Reports started climbing quickly once the issue took hold, pointing to a widespread disruption rather than a handful of isolated complaints.


Outage tracking data shows a clear breakdown of what YouTube users are running into right now. Roughly 41% of reports point to buffering, where videos stall repeatedly instead of playing smoothly. Another 22% describe playback issues entirely, with videos failing to start at all. Crashing accounts for 19% of complaints, while sign in problems make up 11% and video quality issues round out the remaining 6%.

That spread of symptoms suggests the problem is not limited to a single feature. Instead, it appears to be touching multiple parts of how YouTube delivers video to users, from the initial loading process through to actual playback once a video begins streaming.

Why this outage is affecting so many people

Users across multiple cities have reported similar issues within minutes of each other, a pattern that typically points to a server side problem rather than something tied to an individual device, internet provider or region. When outages cluster this tightly in time, it almost always signals that YouTube’s own infrastructure, rather than something on the user end, is behind the disruption.

YouTube has dealt with outages of this kind before, including incidents in 2025 and earlier this year that affected hundreds of thousands of users at a time. Those previous outages were traced to issues ranging from server misconfigurations to problems with the recommendation system that powers the platform’s homepage.

As of this report, no official statement has confirmed the exact cause behind today’s disruption. Past outages have sometimes taken YouTube’s team close to an hour to fully resolve, while others cleared up within 20 to 30 minutes once engineers identified the source of the problem.

The timing of this outage is also significant, as it comes during a period of heavy daytime traffic when schools, offices and households are streaming content simultaneously. That kind of concentrated usage can sometimes amplify the visible impact of a server side issue, since more people are actively trying to load content the moment something goes wrong. Live streams and premieres scheduled for later today could also face delays or rescheduling if the underlying issue is not resolved quickly, since creators often depend on stable uploading and streaming tools to keep scheduled content on track.

How to tell if it is just you or a wider problem

For anyone currently dealing with buffering or crashing, there are a few quick ways to figure out whether the issue is widespread or specific to a single device. Checking an independent outage tracker can confirm whether reports are spiking broadly, rather than just on one phone, tablet or browser.

Restarting the YouTube app or refreshing the browser tab sometimes resolves temporary glitches, though during a confirmed platform wide outage, these steps typically will not fix anything until YouTube resolves the problem on its end. Switching between WiFi and mobile data can also help rule out a local internet issue versus a problem with YouTube itself.

Users who rely on YouTube TV for live programming may notice a separate but related set of issues, since that service runs on much of the same underlying infrastructure as the main YouTube platform. When one experiences disruption, the other sometimes follows shortly after.

Creators who depend on YouTube for daily income have historically voiced the loudest frustration during outages like this one, since even a short disruption can affect view counts, ad revenue and upload scheduling for channels that publish on a tight daily routine.

For now, the safest approach is to wait for an official update rather than repeatedly reinstalling the app or changing account settings, since those steps are unlikely to resolve a problem rooted in YouTube’s own servers. Keeping an eye on outage trackers remains the quickest way to know when service has returned to normal.

data.title: GTA 6 comes as a code in a box, and that’s the problem
data.description:
Physical copies of GTA 6 contain no disc. Instead, the box holds a code that buyers redeem on a PlayStation or Xbox store to download the game. Reports say the physical Standard Edition costs $79.99 and begins shipping Nov. 12, 2026, while the digital-only Ultimate Edition costs $99.99. The format has sparked a debate over ownership, game preservation and the future of physical games.


What is inside the box

According to reports, the physical edition is only available for the Standard Edition. Once a buyer redeems the code, the game is tied to that PlayStation or Xbox account. Reports also say that some physical copies have sold out at major retailers, which suggests that demand is strong even with the limits.


Why ownership is the sticking point

For many players, the core concern is that a physical purchase no longer carries the usual benefits. Disc games can be resold or traded, and they can be played without an online account. A redeemed code cannot be transferred the same way.

GTA 6 ‘An Extended Look’ officially premiered exactly 2 months ago today.

You just had to be there. https://t.co/satAfyaTfv

— GTA 6 Updates (@gtasix_) October 27, 2026

Critics also point to account risk. If a PlayStation or Xbox account is banned, a player could lose access to every digital game on it, including GTA 6. Some retailers have reportedly said they will not stock the game because it does not let buyers truly own what they pay for.

The demand behind the debate

Market data from a mobile research firm estimates that GTA 6 has sold 6.45 million digital pre-orders, generating about $630 million in revenue. A workforce software company reported that time-off requests for the game’s release date rose between 9% and 17%. The numbers show how large the audience is, and why even a code-in-a-box edition attracts buyers.

The hardware question

Some players are also questioning the cost of the hardware needed to play. Secondary-market prices for the PS5 Pro have reportedly reached $1,300 to $1,400, well above the manufacturer’s recommended retail price. One report claims the game may launch with a locked 30 frames per second and no full performance mode on PS5 Pro. That claim is not confirmed, and the publisher has not said whether it is accurate.

What comes next

The debate may reach beyond one game. One report says Sony plans to end disc production starting in 2028. If that happens, GTA 6’s no-disc approach could become a preview of how more publishers handle physical releases. For now, buyers have to decide whether a box with a code is worth the price.

data.title: Apple’s new iPad mini gets its biggest makeover ever
data.description:
Apple’s smallest tablet just got its biggest glow-up yet.


The tech giant unveiled an all-new iPad mini on Monday, Oct. 26, calling it the most significant update in the device’s history. The redesigned tablet features a larger OLED display, a thinner and lighter build, a powerful new A20 Pro chip and, for the first time, protection against water and dust.


Apple says the iPad mini has long been a favorite among a wide range of users, including creators, small business owners, doctors, field service workers and gamers, who appreciate having the full iPad experience in a device that fits in one hand.

A thinner design that can handle a splash

At just 5.4 millimeters thin, the new iPad mini is noticeably slimmer and lighter than the previous generation. It comes in two finishes, a new midnight shade and starlight.

The tablet also carries an IP67 rating, meaning it was tested to withstand dust and submersion in up to 1 meter of water for as long as 30 minutes. Apple notes that the protection could make the tablet a better fit for reading by the pool or working outside on a rainy day, though water resistance can decrease over time with normal wear.

A bigger, brighter screen

The headline feature is the new 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display. Thanks to bezels that are 24% thinner, Apple managed to make the screen bigger without changing the overall size of the device.

OLED technology allows for deeper blacks and richer color. The display reaches a peak brightness of 1,200 nits, which is more than twice as bright as the previous model, and it can dim down to just 1 nit for reading in bed at night. Shoppers can also choose a nano-texture option, previously offered on the iPad Pro, which cuts down on glare in bright settings.

A major boost in power

The A20 Pro chip, built on Apple’s latest 2-nanometer technology, gives the iPad mini a big jump in speed. Apple says the tablet delivers up to 4.5 times faster AI performance and up to 2.7 times faster graphics than the previous version, along with up to 60% faster multitasking performance for everyday jobs like editing photos.

The 512GB model also includes a more advanced Neural Engine with double the processing power of its predecessor, designed for heavier on-device AI work.

Better sound, cameras and connectivity

A new feature Apple calls Acoustic Display routes sound through the screen to deliver punchier bass and clearer highs. The 12MP front camera now sits on the long edge of the tablet, making video calls feel more natural in landscape mode, while the 12MP rear camera records 4K video and gains a new flash for sharper photos and document scans.

The tablet also features Apple’s own N1 wireless chip, which supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Cellular models include the C2 modem, which Apple says offers up to 50% faster data speeds.

Siri gets smarter

The iPad mini runs iPadOS 27, which includes Siri AI, an all-new version of the voice assistant now rolling out in beta. Siri AI can search across a user’s messages, emails and photos, respond to what’s on screen and answer questions on a wide range of topics. Apple notes that Siri AI is not available in the European Union or for users under 13, and some features come with daily usage limits.

Price and release date

Preorders open on Wednesday, Oct. 28, with the tablet arriving in stores on Friday, Nov. 6. The Wi-Fi model starts at $699, while the Wi-Fi and cellular version starts at $849. A new Smart Folio cover sells for $79.

This story was originally reported by Apple Newsroom.
